name: @workjournal/mcp-server

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: List the workspaces the signed-in user owns or belongs to. Returns each workspace with its `slug` — that slug is the first argument to every other tool (e.g. `list_journals(workspace_slug)`). Most users have a single personal workspace named after their account.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Fetch a single workspace by its slug. Slugs are short, hyphenated, globally unique strings (e.g. `acme`, `juliusz-personal`). Use `list_workspaces` first if you do not know the slug.

workspace_slug.description: The workspace slug shown in `list_workspaces`. Example: `acme` or `juliusz-personal`.

tools.name: list_journals
tools.description: List the journals in a workspace that the signed-in user has access to. Pass the workspace slug from `list_workspaces`. Each journal returned has a `slug` you then pass to `get_journal`, `list_entries`, etc. Pass `shared-with-me` as the workspace slug to list journals shared with the user from workspaces they don't own.

workspace_slug.description: Workspace slug from `list_workspaces`. Example: `acme` or `juliusz-personal`. Use the reserved value `shared-with-me` to list journals shared into the caller from other workspaces.

tools.name: get_journal
tools.description: Fetch a single journal by its slug. Returns journal metadata including the active `prompt: { source, name, slug, body, used_by_count }` — `prompt.body` is the journal's writing template: the owner-authored description of how entries in this journal are structured (the system default when no custom template is assigned). It is always populated.

tools.name: rename_journal
tools.description: Rename a journal (display name only). The slug stays the same, so existing links keep working. Use `set_journal_slug` if the user wants to change the URL slug instead.

new_name.description: New display name for the journal.

tools.name: set_journal_slug
tools.description: Change a journal's URL slug. Changing the slug breaks any existing links to this journal — old `<workspace>/<journal>` URLs will return 404. The display name is unaffected; use `rename_journal` for that.

new_slug.description: New URL slug. Lowercase kebab-case. Example: `eng-notes`.

tools.name: update_journal
tools.description: Update a journal's display name and/or description in one call. Both fields are optional — only fields you pass are changed. Pass an empty string for `new_description` to clear it. At least one of `new_name` / `new_description` must be provided. Use `set_journal_slug` to change the URL slug (separate tool because it 404s old links).

new_name.description: New display name. Omit to leave unchanged.

new_description.description: New description. Pass an empty string `""` to clear it (server stores `null`). Omit to leave unchanged.

tools.name: delete_journal
tools.description: Delete a journal and all its entries. Irreversible. Owner-only. Pass workspace and journal slugs.

tools.name: list_entries
tools.description: List recent journal entries for a journal. Returns slim entries (no body). Use `last_entries` or `get_entry` to read entry content. Pass workspace and journal slugs.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default 50, max 100)

tools.name: last_entries
tools.description: Return the N most recent journal entries with their full body content. Pass workspace and journal slugs.

limit.description: Number of recent entries to return (default 1, max 100)

tools.name: get_entry
tools.description: Get a single journal entry by its per-journal index. Pass workspace and journal slugs plus the entry index (e.g. 1, 2, 3 — shown as `#N` in `list_entries` output).

index.description: Per-journal integer index (e.g. 1, 2, 3). Shown as `#N` in `list_entries` output.

tools.name: update_entry
tools.description: Update a journal entry by its per-journal index. All content fields are optional — only fields you pass are changed; the others (and `created_at`, `index`) are unchanged. At least one of `title`, `summary`, `body`, or `tags` must be provided. Passed fields overwrite the stored values (`tags` replaces the whole tag set). Use it to fix or extend an entry while keeping its original timestamp and index. Tag names must be assigned to the journal (see `list_tags`); unknown names are rejected with the valid options in the error. Writes through the Workjournal REST API (https://workjournal.pro/docs/api).

index.description: Per-journal integer index of the entry to update.

title.description: New title (max 80 characters). Omit to leave unchanged.

summary.description: New summary (max 500 characters). Omit to leave unchanged.

body.description: New body markdown. Omit to leave unchanged.

tags.description: Replace the full tag set with this array (Plus+ tier when non-empty; an empty array clears tags and is allowed on any tier). Every name must be **assigned** to this journal — run `list_tags(workspace_slug, journal_slug)` to see the assigned set. Omit to leave the existing tags unchanged.

tools.name: delete_entry
tools.description: Delete a journal entry by its per-journal index. Irreversible. Pass workspace and journal slugs plus the entry index.

index.description: Per-journal integer index of the entry to delete.

tools.name: search_entries
tools.description: Deprecated: stops working after Mon, 30 Nov 2026 23:59:59 GMT. Use `find` with `scope: "wj:<workspace>.<journal>"` instead. Search journal entries in a journal. Returns slim entries — follow up with `get_entry` for the full body. Pass workspace and journal slugs.

tools.name: semantic_search
tools.description: Deprecated: stops working after Mon, 30 Nov 2026 23:59:59 GMT. Use `find` with `scope: "wj:<workspace>.<journal>"` and `type: "rag"` instead. Semantic (RAG) search over a journal — ranks markdown-aware chunks of every entry by cosine similarity against the query embedding. Use this when the user asks about a concept rather than an exact keyword: 'find anything we decided about retry semantics', 'what did we say about pgvector'. Returns the matching CHUNKS (with their parent entry pointer + similarity score), not whole entries — follow up with `get_entry(workspace_slug, journal_slug, entry_index)` to read the full body. Plus+ tier; Free workspaces get a tier-rejection error verbatim.

query.description: Natural-language query to embed and rank against. Phrase as a question or concept (`"retry-with-backoff decision"`) rather than a single keyword — semantic search is at its best when the query carries context.

limit.description: Maximum number of chunks to return. Default 10, capped at 50 server-side (both at the route and inside the RPC).

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search entries across every journal you can see, by keyword (`type: "text"`, the default) or by meaning (`type: "rag"`). Returns one hit per entry, ranked, each with its `wj:` address and `matches` (text: one excerpt with matched words in **bold**; rag: up to 3 chunks). Follow up with `fetch` or `get_entry` for the full body. Without `scope` the search is global: your own workspaces' journals plus journals shared with you, text only. With `scope: "wj:<workspace>"` it covers that workspace's journals you can see (a journal-only contributor sees just the journals shared with them); with `scope: "wj:<workspace>.<journal>"` it searches that one journal. `type: "rag"` requires a workspace or journal scope, owner or member access to its workspace, and the Plus plan; otherwise the error says which condition failed. `limit` counts entries. Scores order hits within one response and can't be compared across types.

query.description: What to search for. text: Postgres websearch syntax (bare words match anywhere, each as a word prefix, so `host` finds "Hostile"; "quoted phrases" match in order; -word excludes). rag: a natural-language phrase or question.

scope.description: Optional workspace or journal address, e.g. `wj:acme` or `wj:acme.engineering`. Omit to search globally (text only). An entry address is rejected.

limit.description: Number of entries to return (default 10, max 50).

offset.description: Entries to skip, for paging. `type: "text"` only; the response carries `total`.

tools.name: create_entry
tools.description: Create a new journal entry in a journal. Pass workspace and journal slugs. The new entry gets an auto-assigned per-journal `index` (e.g. `#7`) returned in the response. Each journal has a writing template (`prompt.body` on `get_journal`) that the journal owner wrote to describe how entries in that journal are structured. Tag names must be ones assigned to the journal (see `list_tags`); unknown names are rejected with an error listing the valid options. Writes through the Workjournal REST API (https://workjournal.pro/docs/api).

title.description: Required. Concise scan-able title (max 80 characters) describing the OUTCOME of this entry — not the process. Example: `Add title field to entries`. If the caller did not supply one, generate it yourself by reviewing what was accomplished.

summary.description: Paragraph-length summary (max 500 characters) describing what was done and why. Used by `last_entries` and search for retrieval context.

body.description: Long-form body — what changed, why it matters, any context.

tags.description: Optional. Tag names to attach (Plus+ tier). Every name must be **assigned** to this journal — run `list_tags(workspace_slug, journal_slug)` to see the assigned set. Unknown names are rejected before the API call with the valid options surfaced in the error.

tools.name: create_journal
tools.description: Create a new journal in a workspace. The slug is auto-derived from `name`; the response includes the new `journal_slug` to use in subsequent calls. Pass the workspace slug to scope creation.

name.description: Display name of the journal (max 100 characters). Example: `Engineering Notes`.

tools.name: list_contributors
tools.description: List contributors of a journal (users with access, including the owner). Pass workspace and journal slugs.

tools.name: delete_contributor
tools.description: Remove a contributor from a journal. Owner-only. Pass workspace and journal slugs plus the contributor user UUID returned by `list_contributors`. (User IDs stay UUIDs — they come from Supabase auth, no slug exists.)

user_id.description: User UUID from `list_contributors` (Supabase auth user ID).

tools.name: list_invitations
tools.description: List invitations for a journal (includes pending, accepted, and revoked). Pass workspace and journal slugs.

tools.name: create_invitation
tools.description: Invite a collaborator to a journal by email. Owner-only. Pass workspace and journal slugs plus the invitee email.

email.description: Email address of the person to invite.

tools.name: delete_invitation
tools.description: Revoke an invitation by its ID. Pass workspace and journal slugs plus the invitation UUID returned by `list_invitations`. (Invitation IDs stay UUIDs — they are internal handles, not user-visible slugs.)

tools.name: export_journal
tools.description: Export a whole journal as a file (JSON, Markdown, CSV, or EPUB) and return a download link with the file name, size, and entry count. The link works in a browser without signing in and expires after 1 hour. The file contents are not included in the response; use `list_entries` or `get_entry` to read entries. EPUB requires a Plus or Pro workspace.

tools.name: list_prompts
tools.description: List the workspace's writing templates (stored as prompts). Returns name, slug, and updated_at for each. Workspace owner only — non-owners get an empty list.

tools.name: get_prompt
tools.description: Fetch a single writing template (prompt) by slug. Returns its full body.

tools.name: create_journal_prompt
tools.description: Create a writing template (prompt) for a journal: inserts the template, adds it to the journal's selectable pool, and makes it the journal's active template, atomically in one call. The template describes how entries in the journal are structured. Requires the `prompt_templates` tier feature (Pro). Body cap 10K chars; name cap 80 chars. If `slug` is omitted, it is derived from `name`. The reserved slug `default` is rejected. Writes through the Workjournal REST API (https://workjournal.pro/docs/api).

journal_slug.description: Journal slug from `list_journals`. The new prompt is added to this journal's pool and immediately selected. Example: `engineering-notes`.

slug.description: Optional URL slug. Lowercase kebab-case. Example: `project-style`.

tools.name: update_prompt
tools.description: Update a writing template's (prompt's) name and/or body; passed fields overwrite the stored values. The slug is stable, so renaming does not change the URL. Requires `custom_prompt`. Writes through the Workjournal REST API (https://workjournal.pro/docs/api).

tools.name: delete_prompt
tools.description: Delete a writing template (prompt). Cascades to remove it from any journal pool and resets `selected_prompt_id` on any journals selecting it back to the system default. Requires `prompt_templates` (Pro).

tools.name: select_journal_prompt
tools.description: Set the journal's active writing template (prompt). The target template must be in the journal's pool (or the global default — pass `prompt_slug = 'default'` to select it). Requires `custom_prompt`. Affects only the active selection — the journal's pool membership is untouched.

tools.name: unselect_journal_prompt
tools.description: Reset the journal's active writing template (prompt) to the system default. Equivalent to calling `select_journal_prompt` with `prompt_slug = 'default'`. Requires `custom_prompt`. The journal's pool is untouched.

tools.name: list_tags
tools.description: List tags in a workspace. Without `journal_slug`: returns the full workspace registry. With `journal_slug`: filters to tags assigned to that journal (the set entries in that journal can carry). Read-only — available to any workspace member (Free or paid). Each tag has `name` and `description`; with `journal_slug`, only assigned rows are listed. Tier gating applies only to create / assign / write operations.

journal_slug.description: Optional. Filter to tags assigned to this journal — the set usable on entries here.

tools.name: get_tag
tools.description: Fetch a single tag from the workspace registry by name. With `journal_slug`, also reports whether the tag is currently assigned to that journal.

journal_slug.description: Optional. When set, the output reports whether the tag is assigned to this journal.

tools.name: create_tag
tools.description: Create a new tag in the workspace registry. The new tag is NOT auto-assigned to any journal — follow up with `assign_tag` to make it usable in a specific journal. Plus+ tier. Names are kebab-case (max 50); descriptions optional, max 200 chars.

name.description: Tag name. Lowercase kebab-case, alphanumeric. Example: `decision`.

description.description: Optional description (max 200 chars). Helps disambiguate synonyms for AI agents in closed-enum write paths.

tools.name: update_tag
tools.description: Rename a tag or replace its description. Renaming cascades to every entry in every journal the tag is assigned to. Description may be cleared. Not tier-gated — downgraded workspaces can still tidy up.

description.description: New description (max 200). Pass null to clear an existing description. Optional.

tools.name: delete_tag
tools.description: Delete a tag from the workspace registry. Cascades to remove the tag from every entry in every journal the tag was assigned to. Not tier-gated.

tools.name: assign_tag
tools.description: Assign a tag from the workspace registry to a journal. Entries in that journal can then carry the tag via `write_entry` / `update_entry`. Plus+ tier — assignment is what unlocks the tag for entry use.

tag_name.description: Existing tag in the workspace registry.

tools.name: unassign_tag
tools.description: Unassign a tag from a journal. Cascades to strip the tag from every existing entry in that journal. The tag itself stays in the workspace registry — other journals are unaffected. Not tier-gated.

tag_name.description: Tag currently assigned to the journal.

tools.name: upload_attachment
tools.description: Upload a file (image or PDF, max 5 MiB) as an attachment in a journal by passing its bytes as base64. Works on every surface including the hosted remote server. Returns the attachment id and a content URL you can embed in an entry as `![name](url)` or link to. Per-workspace storage quota applies by tier. On the local stdio server, prefer `upload_attachment_from_path` to avoid base64-encoding a file you already have on disk.

filename.description: Filename with a supported extension (.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.pdf); the content type is inferred from it. Example: `diagram.png`.

data.description: The raw file bytes encoded as standard base64 (not a URL, not a data: URI, not the file text). Must decode to ≤5 MiB.

tools.name: list_attachments
tools.description: List the file attachments in a journal — id, filename, type, size, content URL, and the indices of entries that reference each one. Read-only.

tools.name: delete_attachment
tools.description: Delete an attachment from a journal by id. Removes the stored file and unlinks it from any entries that referenced it. Only the uploader or the journal owner can delete.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search across the user's accessible workjournal entries (their own workspaces' journals plus journals shared with them), ranked across journals, up to 50 entries. Returns a JSON object `{results: [{id, title, text, url}]}` where each `id` is a workjournal address of the form `wj:<workspace>.<journal>#<index>` you can pass to `fetch` for the full entry body. Stable within a session, but not across workspace or journal slug renames (`set_journal_slug` breaks old ids the same way it breaks old web URLs). Use as the primary discovery tool when the user asks about something they've previously logged. Uses Postgres websearch syntax: bare words match anywhere, each as a word prefix (`host` finds "Hostile"); double-quoted phrases match in order. For a workspace scope, paging, or semantic (RAG) search, use `find`.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch the full body of a single workjournal entry by the `id` returned from `search`. The id is a workjournal address of the form `wj:<workspace>.<journal>#<index>` (e.g. `wj:acme.engineering-notes#42`); the legacy `<workspace>/<journal>/<index>` form is also accepted. Returns a JSON object `{id, title, text, url, metadata}` where `text` is the entry's full markdown content (title + summary + body).

id.description: Entry id from `search` results, in the form `wj:<workspace>.<journal>#<index>` (e.g. `wj:acme.engineering-notes#42`). The legacy `<workspace>/<journal>/<index>` form is also accepted.

tools.name: auth_login
tools.description: Start the Workjournal login flow. Returns a URL the user should open in any browser to sign in. After signing in, the user copies the 8-character code shown on the page and the agent calls `auth_complete` with that code. Use this when `auth_status` reports unauthenticated, or when other tools fail with "Authentication required".

tools.name: auth_complete
tools.description: Finish the Workjournal login flow by submitting the 8-character code displayed on the sign-in page after the user has approved access. Must be preceded by `auth_login`.

code.description: The 8-character code shown on the workjournal.pro sign-in page after approval.

tools.name: auth_status
tools.description: Report whether the Workjournal MCP server has valid credentials on disk.

tools.name: upload_attachment_from_path
tools.description: Upload a local file (image or PDF, max 5 MiB) as an attachment in a journal, reading it from a path on the machine running this MCP server. Returns the attachment id and a content URL you can embed in an entry as `![name](url)` or link to. Per-workspace storage quota applies by tier. Local stdio only — the hosted remote server has no filesystem; use `upload_attachment` with base64 there.

file_path.description: Absolute or relative path to a local .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.pdf file (≤5 MiB).

instructions: Workjournal MCP server. If `auth_status` reports unauthenticated, call `auth_login` to get a sign-in URL, ask the user to open it and paste the 8-character code back, then call `auth_complete` with the code. After that the regular tools (list_journals, create_entry, etc.) work.
